quotes.q: But we're here today because PGM is facing a grave legitimacy crisis. Frustrations are mounting.
quotes.tenet: PJM faces a legitimacy crisis that governance reform must address.

quotes.q: Put plainly, market participants have lost confidence in PGM's decision-making abilities.
quotes.tenet: Market participants no longer trust PJM to make decisions.

quotes.q: We need PJM to act decisively and reinstill the confidence in investors that is necessary for the region to attract the billions and capital that we need to build generation
quotes.tenet: PJM must act decisively to draw the capital needed for new generation.

quotes.q: Families in the PJM footprint should not be asked to shoulder the financial burden of processes that are slow, fragmented, or opaque.
quotes.tenet: Ratepayers should not pay for slow or opaque PJM processes.

quotes.q: We are looking for the reforms that are clearly articulated, evaluated, and we want them to be filed under section 205 or section 206 as appropriate.
quotes.tenet: Stakeholders should bring specific reforms ready to file under section 205 or 206.

quotes.q: And if we can't all agree, then FK will be in a position where we may have to do it for you.
quotes.tenet: FERC will impose governance reforms if stakeholders cannot agree.

quotes.q: After we receive these postconference comments, we are going to direct the commission's dispute resolution service to convene a forum in September.
quotes.tenet: A structured FERC-run forum in September will aim to finalize a reform package.

quotes.q: If the stakeholders cannot reach a set of credible meaningful reforms or an agreement in principle by the end of September, then this commission is not going to hesitate to use the full extent of our legal authority
quotes.tenet: FERC will use its full authority if no agreement emerges by September.

quotes.q: First, I agree that states need an enhanced role in the governance process and this must be a real role with teeth.
quotes.tenet: States need a real governance role with enforcement power.

quotes.q: Third, I'm interested in discussing pathways either in the stakeholder process or in another venue to amplify state input on issues related to resource adequacy.
quotes.tenet: States should have more input on resource adequacy.

quotes.q: States are critical partners in ensuring in ensuring resource adequacy because states are ultimately responsible for citing and permitting the generation and transmission that is needed
quotes.tenet: States share resource adequacy because they site and permit generation and transmission.

quotes.q: We also need states help on curtailment priority, otherwise known as emergency load reduction rules for large loads.
quotes.tenet: States must set curtailment priority rules for large loads.

quotes.q: And we need states to put in place cost allocation rules for back for a backs stop auction if and when we have one.
quotes.tenet: States must set backstop auction cost allocation rules.

quotes.q: PJM will not succeed without our state colleagues also ensuring that we timely get generation and transmission built.
quotes.tenet: PJM cannot succeed unless states speed generation and transmission siting.

quotes.q: Mr. Mills, uh, we need the cost allocation in place for that now and the fact that it's not here is creating dramatic uncertainty.
quotes.tenet: Backstop auction cost allocation is overdue and creates uncertainty.

quotes.q: for me uh the highest priority issue is that we're 60 6,800 megawatts short uh 2 years from now.
quotes.tenet: PJM's 6,800 megawatt shortfall is the top priority.

quotes.q: That's why the state role is so important. That's why we need our state regulators working with us to do the cost allocation, to do the curtailment priority
quotes.tenet: State regulators must handle cost allocation and curtailment priority.

quotes.q: Even with market intervention, we still have sky-high prices. And last week was the second time that the auction failed to secure enough capacity to meet the reserve threshold in PJM.
quotes.tenet: PJM prices stay very high and the auction again fell short.

quotes.q: the pace and scale of large load growth is well beyond an ordinary demand spike.
quotes.tenet: Large load growth exceeds what markets are built to absorb.

quotes.q: First, PJM's unique stakeholder process and system of voting may work in many contexts, but it hasn't led to results in some of the most consequential questions PJM is grappling with now.
quotes.tenet: PJM's voting process has not delivered on the biggest questions.

quotes.q: State representation on the nominating committee seems an obvious step forward uh for me in this area.
quotes.tenet: States should sit on the board nominating committee.

quotes.q: So let's not shy away today from whether an advisory stakeholder process, which is almost unique from other markets, is the right path forward for PJM.
quotes.tenet: An advisory stakeholder process deserves serious consideration for PJM.

quotes.q: I think we've got basically three buckets that have been proposed, right? The first is states involvement in board selection.
quotes.tenet: State reform proposals fall into board selection, direction and filing rights.

quotes.q: There's a number of themes that came out of today obviously and board independence I think is probably the phrase we heard more than any others.
quotes.tenet: Board independence was the dominant theme of the conference.

quotes.q: you know, from my point, I find it pretty persuasive to have meaningful role for the states in that area.
quotes.tenet: States deserve a meaningful role in choosing the board.

quotes.q: we've got to figure out what happens when we can't get to consensus. We just have to figure out how to break through the stalemates.
quotes.tenet: PJM needs a way to decide when consensus fails.

quotes.q: The way I see this is the problems in PJM's market is actually a collective problem and it needs to be solved collectively.
quotes.tenet: PJM's market problems need a collective solution, not blame.

quotes.q: PGM happens to be ground zero for global data center development at least the first in the US have all contributed to the recent recent resource adequacy challenges.
quotes.tenet: Data center growth in PJM contributed to its resource adequacy problems.

quotes.q: not every problem at PGM will be fixed through changes of the governance structure.
quotes.tenet: Governance reform will not fix every PJM problem.

quotes.q: But what is important is that these process related challenges the answer to these challenges is swift decision making.
quotes.tenet: Swift decision making is the answer to PJM's process problems.

quotes.q: When we discuss governance issues, I support, just like I supported in order 1920, strong state representation, I support having more representation from consumer advocates as well
quotes.tenet: PJM governance needs strong state and consumer advocate representation.

quotes.q: in some ways you might not make the perfect decisions. But we need to make those decisions and then enhance them as we go along.
quotes.tenet: PJM should decide quickly and refine decisions over time.

quotes.q: So I do believe that states must have some way of interacting and actually decisionmaking rights whether that's a 205 jump ball type of rights or some other way
quotes.tenet: States need real decision-making rights, such as jump ball filing.

quotes.q: I feel like communication has has broken down communication with the states and maybe multiple entities of the states and m maybe communications with stakeholders even
quotes.tenet: PJM's communication with states and stakeholders has broken down.

quotes.q: there's got to be a you know timeline on the decisions on the stakeholders. It can't just be forever stakeholdering and then PJM and its board has to make certain decisions and make the filing.
quotes.tenet: Stakeholder deliberation needs a deadline, then the board must file.

quotes.q: To me it's the interconnection process. It's the transmission planning process which I think the states need a role and a voice in.
quotes.tenet: States need a voice in interconnection and transmission planning.

quotes.q: I've said publicly that the status quo is untenable and that seems to be the public perception, the perception of the Americans that rely on PJM
quotes.tenet: The status quo at PJM is untenable.

quotes.q: PGM is the is confronting rapid large lo grow growth rapid large load growth from the prolification of data centers, re-industrialization.
quotes.tenet: PJM faces rapid large load growth from data centers and industry.

quotes.q: PGM has a binding stakeholder process that is untransparent and designed to protect the interest of those who profit.
quotes.tenet: PJM's binding stakeholder process protects those who profit.

quotes.q: if the players on the field do not like the calls that the referees make, guess what? They can replace those referees that are more beneficial to ones that were make going to make the calls that are more beneficial to their areas.
quotes.tenet: Stakeholders who can replace the board undermine its independence.

quotes.q: I've told you previously that I expect all parties here to have settlement authority and to make your positions known.
quotes.tenet: Parties must come with authority to settle.

quotes.q: I'd like to see an agreement in principle for an instrument with common sense reforms that are negotiated through this technical conference.
quotes.tenet: An agreement in principle on reforms is expected by end of summer.

quotes.q: I don't see us getting around this without breaking the chains of making the stakeholder process advisory.
quotes.tenet: PJM's stakeholder process should become advisory.

quotes.q: But you know where we stand right now, where we sit, if we don't change, there's a 100% chance of failure.
quotes.tenet: Without change, PJM will fail.

quotes.q: And if we don't get that action out of PJM, we will use every single legal authority within us and maybe some more to figure that out.
quotes.tenet: FERC will use every legal authority if PJM does not act.
